summary.text: A 68-year-old man with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer had a biopsy showing extracapsular prostate cancer with Gleason Score 9. First 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT in February 2020 showed widespread sclerotic skeletal and lymphatic metastases, and he had extensive bone discomfort, particularly in the left upper limb. Prostatectomy was not recommended.

Leuprorelin/bicalutamide and docetaxel were initiated; docetaxel was discontinued after 3 months due to neutropenia and leukopenia and abiraterone was prescribed. The left shoulder received palliative radiotherapy for limited left arm range of motion, and androgen blockade and deprivation therapy continued up until February 2021, when 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT revealed PSMA-avid prostate cancer with lymphatic and sclerotic skeletal metastases.

He was sent to the clinic for 177Lu-PSMA therapy, 7.4 GBq per cycle at 6-week intervals, for ten cycles. Bone pain significantly decreased after the first treatment, transdermal analgesic patches and opioid-derived medications were discontinued after 4 cycles, and the prescription for pain relief was stopped after cycle 8. Laboratory tests showed no hematological or renal toxicities.

Following 10 therapy cycles total serum PSA decreased to 2.71 ng/ml and decreased by 99% from baseline, and 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT in March 2022 showed the prostate cancer had completely disappeared with response at every disease site. The authors report a dramatic response and well-tolerated therapy. The patient died unexpectedly in 2022 from cardiovascular failure induced by COVID-19.
